title: What the Gut Lets Go
endLine: When capture is nearly complete, small slips multiply what leaves.

scenes.tts: Nine to eleven litres of fluid enter your gut each day. A couple of hundred grams of stool leave. Where did that water go, and what decides how much leaves?
scenes.narration: Nine to eleven litres of fluid enter your gut each day. A couple of hundred grams of stool leave. Where did that water go, and what decides how much leaves?
scenes.caption: Nine to eleven litres of fluid enter your gut each day. A couple of hundred grams of stool leave. Where did that water go, and what decides how much leaves?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: water CYAN drops; sodium BLUE dots; chloride GREEN dots; sugar GOLD dots; the sodium pump RED; cholera toxin and cyclic AMP MAGENTA; ledger bars and numbers WHITE; gut-lining cells pale grey fill. LAYOUT: LEFT 68% of the frame is one long cut-away gut tube running left to right across the middle, filling about 60% of frame height (schematic, no anatomy detail). Its lower wall is a row of finger-shaped villi with narrow pits (crypts) between them; under the wall runs a dark band labelled 'blood' with a slow left-to-right flow of faint dots. At the left end a wide mouth labelled 'in'; at the right end a narrow outlet labelled 'out'. RIGHT 32%: the LEDGER, kept all film: a tall WHITE bar 'load' on a scale of 0 to 12 litres a day, a separate small WHITE bar 'stool water' on its own magnified scale of 0 to 0.25 litres a day, and a round dial 'captured' below them. Tag 'teaching numbers' under the ledger, kept all film. Hook motion: a thick stream of CYAN drops pours in at the left mouth and travels right along the tube; most drops sink down through the wall into the blood band and are carried away; only a thin drip leaves at the right outlet. The load bar fills toward the top while the stool-water bar barely rises. On the question, white text across the top: 'Where did the water go?'

Title 'What the Gut Lets Go' fades in over the top of the tube for 2 s while the question text fades out. CYAN drops keep pouring in, sinking through the wall and dripping from the outlet. Ledger bars reset to empty.

scenes.tts: About two litres is what you drink. Your own secretions add roughly seven to nine more: saliva, gastric juice, bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal fluid. About ninety-nine percent is taken back.
scenes.narration: About 2 litres is what you drink. Your own secretions add roughly 7 to 9 more: saliva, gastric juice, bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal fluid. About 99 percent is taken back.
scenes.caption: About 2 litres is what you drink. Your own secretions add roughly 7 to 9 more: saliva, gastric juice, bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal fluid. About 99 percent is taken back.
scenes.visual: On 'what you drink', a CYAN segment fills the load bar to 2 litres, labelled 'drink: 2'. On 'secretions', five small side inlets open along the top of the tube and add their own CYAN streams; a second, slightly paler CYAN segment stacks on the load bar from 2 up to 11 litres, labelled 'secretions: 9 (round)'. The total reads 'load: 11 L a day'. On 'taken back', the stream of drops sinking through the wall into the blood band thickens, and the dial swings to '99%'.

scenes.tts: So what leaves is whatever was not taken back. Stool water equals the load times one minus the fraction reabsorbed. With round numbers, eleven litres times one percent is about a tenth of a litre a day.
scenes.narration: So what leaves is whatever was not taken back. Stool water = load × (1 − fraction reabsorbed). With round numbers, 11 litres × 1 percent ≈ 0.11 litres a day.
scenes.caption: So what leaves is whatever was not taken back. Stool water = load × (1 − fraction reabsorbed). With round numbers, 11 litres × 1 percent ≈ 0.11 litres a day.
scenes.visual: The drip at the right outlet is highlighted. Along the bottom of the frame the rule writes itself in WHITE, size 34: 'stool water = load × (1 − captured)'. On 'eleven litres times one percent', the 11 L load bar slides a thin 1% sliver off its top across to the stool-water bar, which fills to 0.11 on its magnified scale, labelled '0.11 L a day'. The rest of the drops keep sinking into the blood band.

scenes.tts: Try two changes. Add one litre to the load, and keep ninety-nine percent capture. Or keep the load, and capture one point less. Which raises stool water more?
scenes.narration: Try two changes. Add 1 litre to the load, and keep 99 percent capture. Or keep the load, and capture 1 point less. Which raises stool water more?
scenes.caption: Try two changes. Add 1 litre to the load, and keep 99 percent capture. Or keep the load, and capture 1 point less. Which raises stool water more?
scenes.visual: Two option cards slide in above the ledger, side by side: 'A: load 12 L, 99%' and 'B: load 11 L, 98%'. On option A, a ghost extra litre glows above the load bar; on option B, the dial's needle twitches toward 98 and back. The stool-water bar stays at 0.11. Question card across the top in white: 'Which raises stool water more?'

Predict pause. The question card and both option cards stay. Drops keep pouring in slowly and sinking through the wall; the drip at the outlet continues; the ledger holds at 11 L, 99%, 0.11 L. No other change.

scenes.tts: The extra litre adds only about a hundredth of a litre, in proportion to the load. One point less capture takes stool water from eleven hundredths of a litre to twenty-two. It doubles.
scenes.narration: The extra litre adds only about a hundredth of a litre, in proportion to the load. One point less capture takes stool water from 0.11 litres to 0.22. It doubles.
scenes.caption: The extra litre adds only about a hundredth of a litre, in proportion to the load. One point less capture takes stool water from 0.11 litres to 0.22. It doubles.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. Option A plays first: the load bar grows to 12 L, the inflow thickens slightly, and the stool-water bar rises from 0.11 to 0.12, labelled 'A: 0.12'. Reset. Option B plays: load back at 11 L, the dial drops to 98%, the outlet drip visibly doubles, and the stool-water bar rises from 0.11 to 0.22, labelled 'B: 0.22'. On 'It doubles', a WHITE bracket beside the bar reads 'x 2'. Both results stay side by side as small marks on the stool-water scale.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. What leaves is a small residue of a large flow. When capture is nearly complete, that residue is very sensitive to it. A bigger load raises it only in proportion.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. What leaves is a small residue of a large flow. When capture is nearly complete, that residue is very sensitive to it. A bigger load raises it only in proportion.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. What leaves is a small residue of a large flow. When capture is nearly complete, that residue is very sensitive to it. A bigger load raises it only in proportion.
scenes.visual: Reset the ledger to 11 L, 99%, 0.11 L. On 'small residue of a large flow', the thick inflow at the left and the thin drip at the right pulse together. On 'very sensitive', the dial needle wobbles slightly and the outlet drip swells and shrinks with each wobble. On 'only in proportion', the inflow widens a little and the drip grows only a little. Label at the top: 'residue = load × (1 − captured)'.

scenes.tts: Who adds to the load, and who captures? In pits called crypts, a sodium pump and N K C C one pack chloride into the cell. When the channel C F T R opens, chloride pours into the gut. Sodium follows between the cells, and water follows both.
scenes.narration: Who adds to the load, and who captures? In pits called crypts, a sodium pump and NKCC1 pack chloride into the cell. When the channel CFTR opens, chloride pours into the gut. Sodium follows between the cells, and water follows both.
scenes.caption: Who adds to the load, and who captures? In pits called crypts, a sodium pump and NKCC1 pack chloride into the cell. When the channel CFTR opens, chloride pours into the gut. Sodium follows between the cells, and water follows both.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into the tube wall until one villus and the crypt beside it fill about 70% of frame height; the ledger stays at the right, smaller. Cells are pale grey blocks lining the crypt; gut above, blood band below. On 'sodium pump', a RED pump cartoon appears on the base of a crypt cell; on 'N K C C one', a carrier cartoon labelled 'NKCC1' appears beside it on the base and draws GREEN chloride dots into the cell, which crowd inside. On 'C F T R', a channel on the gut-facing top of the cell, labelled 'CFTR', swings open: GREEN dots stream out into the crypt and up into the gut. On 'Sodium follows', BLUE dots slip up through the gap between two crypt cells; on 'water follows both', CYAN drops follow them out. The ledger's load bar edges up slightly.

scenes.tts: On the fingers called villi, the flow runs the other way. N H E three and a partner exchanger bring sodium chloride in. S G L T one carries sodium in with sugar. Water follows the absorbed salt.
scenes.narration: On the fingers called villi, the flow runs the other way. NHE3 and a partner exchanger bring sodium chloride in. SGLT1 carries sodium in with sugar. Water follows the absorbed salt.
scenes.caption: On the fingers called villi, the flow runs the other way. NHE3 and a partner exchanger bring sodium chloride in. SGLT1 carries sodium in with sugar. Water follows the absorbed salt.
scenes.visual: Camera slides up the villus beside the crypt. On its gut-facing top, two linked exchanger cartoons labelled 'NHE3 + partner' take in BLUE and GREEN dots together. Beside them a turnstile labelled 'SGLT1' turns: BLUE dots and GOLD dots pass in together. On 'Water follows', CYAN drops move from the gut through the villus into the blood band below. Arrows: crypt arrow pointing up into the gut, villus arrow pointing down into blood.

scenes.tts: Secretion mostly happens in the crypts, and absorption mostly on the villi, though one cell can do both. Stool water is the difference. Behind them stands the colon, which can absorb up to four to five litres a day.
scenes.narration: Secretion mostly happens in the crypts, and absorption mostly on the villi, though one cell can do both. Stool water is the difference. Behind them stands the colon, which can absorb up to 4 to 5 litres a day.
scenes.caption: Secretion mostly happens in the crypts, and absorption mostly on the villi, though one cell can do both. Stool water is the difference. Behind them stands the colon, which can absorb up to 4 to 5 litres a day.
scenes.visual: The crypt's up-arrow (labelled 'mostly secrete') and the villus's down-arrow (labelled 'mostly absorb') glow together; on 'one cell can do both', one villus cell briefly shows a small CFTR channel beside its NHE3 pair. Pull back to the full tube. On 'the difference', the drip at the outlet pulses. On 'the colon', the last stretch of the tube before the outlet brightens, labelled 'colon: up to 4-5 L a day', and draws extra CYAN drops down into the blood band. Ledger back at 11 L, 99%, 0.11 L.

scenes.tts: Cholera pulls on both terms at once. Its toxin jams a G protein in the on position, so cells keep making cyclic A M P. In the crypts, that opens C F T R, and the load rises. On the villi, it slows N H E three, and capture falls.
scenes.narration: Cholera pulls on both terms at once. Its toxin jams a G protein in the on position, so cells keep making cyclic AMP. In the crypts, that opens CFTR, and the load rises. On the villi, it slows NHE3, and capture falls.
scenes.caption: Cholera pulls on both terms at once. Its toxin jams a G protein in the on position, so cells keep making cyclic AMP. In the crypts, that opens CFTR, and the load rises. On the villi, it slows NHE3, and capture falls.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes back in to the same crypt and villus. MAGENTA toxin chips drift in the gut and settle on the lining cells (the bacterium itself stays in the gut). On 'G protein', a switch icon inside each cell labelled 'G protein' clicks to 'on' and stays stuck; MAGENTA 'cyclic AMP' glow fills the cells. On 'opens C F T R', the crypt's CFTR swings wide: GREEN, BLUE and CYAN pour out into the gut, and the ledger's load bar rises above 11 L (schematic, no number). On 'slows N H E three', the NHE3 pair on the villus slows and dims, fewer CYAN drops cross into blood, and the dial needle drops below 99% (schematic, no number). SGLT1 keeps turning at its usual pace, unlabelled and unhighlighted. Tag 'schematic' beside the ledger.

scenes.tts: So the gut works near an edge. It takes back nearly everything. So a small slip in any capturing step shows up many times over in what leaves.
scenes.narration: So the gut works near an edge. It takes back nearly everything. So a small slip in any capturing step shows up many times over in what leaves.
scenes.caption: So the gut works near an edge. It takes back nearly everything. So a small slip in any capturing step shows up many times over in what leaves.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full tube world; the toxin and MAGENTA glow fade and the ledger returns to 11 L, 99%, 0.11 L. On 'takes back nearly everything', the thick stream of drops sinking through the wall into the blood band glows. On 'a small slip', the dial needle dips a hair and the outlet drip swells visibly; then the needle returns and the drip shrinks back.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (CYAN drops pouring in, sinking through the wall, a thin drip at the outlet). Large white text, centred: 'When capture is nearly complete, small slips multiply what leaves.'
